problems.title: Abelian subgroup covers
problems.summary: How many abelian subgroups are needed to cover a group with a bounded pairwise-noncommuting set?
problems.question: Write a(G) for the minimum abelian-subgroup cover size and omega(G) for the maximum pairwise-noncommuting set size. The global function h(n) takes the supremum over ALL groups with omega(G) <= n.
problems.boundary: No solution of the headline problem is claimed here. Finite censuses, ordinary proofs and Lean-checked witnesses have different scopes. External open/solved status is not inferred from repository labels.
problems.next_question: Does a three-coordinate alternating map on F2^5 have a cover number strictly larger than its noncommuting clique number?
problems.falsifier: An independently checked matching cover and clique does not settle the whole class. One certified gap decides existence positively; a complete exclusion needs its own proof or complete domain.

problems.title: Sparse rulers and difference bases
problems.summary: Find small sets of marks whose differences cover every required distance.
problems.question: For a ruler on {0,...,N}, every distance 1,...,N must occur as a difference of two marks. The original experiment suite remains in the repository root.
problems.boundary: Heuristic candidates are not optimality certificates. The continuous autocorrelation parameter tau is not the discrete sparse-ruler limit. No new #170 numerical or asymptotic result is added by this navigation release.
problems.next_question: Audit a saved discrete candidate together with its stated lower bound before promoting it from a search output to an exact result.
problems.falsifier: A missing distance invalidates a complete-ruler claim. A candidate without a matching lower bound is not an optimum.

problems.title: Modular distinct subset sums
problems.summary: Understand the structure of n-element sets with all subset sums distinct modulo 2^n+5.
problems.question: Compare admissible sets with signed unit dilations of {1,2,4,...,2^(n-1)}. This is a separately tracked research branch; no unverified Erdős problem number is assigned.
problems.boundary: The certified n=6 result is not a proof for every n. Sign reduction, completeness and the independent checker are part of the finite claim.
problems.next_question: At n=7 and modulus 133, can an admissible set require more than one replacement to reach a signed, unit-scaled powers-of-two set?
problems.falsifier: One fully verified set at replacement distance at least two refutes the proposed all-n pattern. An incomplete search with no counterexample does not prove it.

results.title: Modulus 69: complete n=6 case
results.scope: 4,224 admissible sets; each is within one replacement of signed unit-scaled powers of two. No all-n theorem.

problems.title: Three unit fractions / Erdős–Straus
problems.summary: Identify exact first denominators for strictly increasing positive three-unit-fraction representations of 4/n.
problems.question: For every n>2, can 4/n be written as 1/x+1/y+1/z with strictly increasing positive integer denominators? The registered result determines the smallest first denominator only for an explicit infinite composite family.
problems.boundary: The 2013 two-term fraction criterion is known. An exact scoped first-denominator family is not a general solution; present literature priority is unchecked and no Lean proof is claimed.
problems.next_question: For prime n congruent to 1 modulo 24, can one prove an explicit residue subclass where the smallest allowed x is excluded and the next x has a symbolic positive ordered construction?
problems.falsifier: An explicit prime n in the proposed subclass lacking the predicted x1 construction, or a correct smaller x0 witness, refutes that restricted claim. A finite prime list does not prove residue coverage.

results.title: Minimum first denominator on an infinite square family
results.scope: All n=t², t positive divisible by 7 with every prime factor 1 modulo 3; least ordered positive first denominator equals (n+7)/4. No global conjecture solved.
